items.title: EBA Founder Eniola Omoniyi Calls for More Strategic Brand Building Following NAC 2026 - THISDAYLIVE
items.raw_summary: Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google Follow us on Google Eniola Omoniyi, popularly known as Eniivy and Iyalode, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of ENI Brand Architect Limited (EBA), has emphasised the need for businesses and marketing communications agencies to move beyond brand visibility and focus on strategy, credibility and measurable business outcomes. Reflecting on discussions at the 2026 National Advertising Conference (NAC) in Abuja, Eniola noted that the changing expectations of consumers and businesses require a broader approach to brand building and marketing communications. The conference, themed “Repositioning the Marketing Communications Industry for the Next Frontier,” brought together advertising professionals, business leaders, regulators and other industry stakeholders to examine the future of Nigeria’s marketing communications industry. For Eniola, one of the important conversations emerging from the conference is the distinction between attracting attention and building a business that can sustain consumer trust. “Visibility gets people to notice your brand, but credibility gives them a reason to trust it. Businesses must understand that being seen is different from being chosen. A successful campaign can attract attention, but what happens after that attention is what determines whether people become customers and whether those customers return,” she said. She explained that businesses must pay greater attention to the relationship between brand promises, customer experience and actual service delivery. According to her, a business can invest significantly in advertising, public relations and digital marketing, but those investments may deliver limited long-term value if its positioning is unclear or the customer experience contradicts its communication. Eniola also highlighted the changing responsibilities of marketing communications agencies, noting that businesses increasingly require partners who understand their commercial objectives and can contribute to solving problems beyond promotional activities. “An agency should be able to ask what problem a business is trying to solve, who it is trying to reach, what needs to change and how success will be measured. We have to move beyond simply delivering campaigns and start paying closer attention to the business objectives those campaigns are expected to achieve,” she added. As Founder and CEO of ENI Brand Architect, a company providing integrated business strategy, brand development, communications, creative production and execution services, Eniola’s perspective draws from working with organisationsacross different sectors and stages of business development. Her experience also extends to broadcasting, event production, partnerships and community engagement. She serves as Head of Events and Sponsorships at Lounge Network and is the convener of The Eniivy Experience, a community platform established in 2018. Drawing from these experiences, she identified strategic positioning, consumer understanding, consistency and adaptability as important considerations for businesses seeking sustainable growth. She noted that brands must understand the people they serve, remain consistent in their promises and delivery, and adapt to changing market conditions without losing the identity that makes them recognisable. For communications agencies, Eniola believes the industry’s next stage of development will require stronger business understanding, greater accountability and a willingness to challenge approaches that prioritise activity over outcomes. Reflecting on NAC 2026, she maintained that repositioning Nigeria’s marketing communications industry should extend beyond conversations about emerging technologies, new platforms and changing consumer behaviour. It must also influence how businesses define their objectives, how agencies develop solutions and how success is evaluated. For Eniola, the future of brand building lies in connecting strategy with execution and ensuring that every communication effort contributes to a clear business purpose.
